display.text: The quantity representing probability in a continuous density model. The area between a and b equals P(a ≤ X ≤ b), and the total area is 1.
The function F(x) = P(X ≤ x), giving probability accumulated up to x. For a continuous distribution, P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = F(b) − F(a). Abbreviated CDF.
A continuous distribution with a symmetric, bell-shaped density, specified by its mean μ and standard deviation σ.
Probability per unit of the measurement scale. A density histogram's bar height is the interval probability divided by its width, so the bar's area equals that probability.

A nonnegative function f(x) representing a continuous distribution, with total area 1. Probability over an interval is the area under the curve there, rather than its height at a point. Abbreviated PDF; also called a probability density curve.
